notes.1: Close. Misregistration is framed around the type, and the inks are named as teal and coral rather than chosen per film.
notes.2: Multiply inks, stepped halftone, speckle fixed to the paper and the knockout trap are right. But misregistration is not a per-plate property of everything printed (only type is offset), plates get no separate screen angles, and the 'at most two plates per area, one of them a tint' rule is missing.
notes.3: Riso colour logic holds: spot inks, tints by halftone, overprint as the darkest value, cream paper, no black. But it fixes teal + coral and confines coral to a ~3 % accent that never fills a field.
notes.4: Double-hit title and roller entrance match, but subtitles lose the paper-white knockout strip; 'never a boxed caption' contradicts it.
notes.5: On twos, fixed per-shot registration and the constant-speed roller are right. But the registration kick on accents and the drift/snap are missing, though the film kicks at 9.5 s. 'step(t, 12) for everything' would also step camera moves, which the original keeps on ones.
notes.6: Locked composition, roller transitions and no dissolves match. The moving-camera vocabulary (tracking, push into halftone, match cuts) is absent but unshown.
notes.7: Consistent. The print machine's own sounds (drum ka-chunk, feed) are reduced to a roller swish.
notes.8: The moves are generic pulls and rises. The plate moves the film used are missed or misread: the third colour where two inks meet (the sun's reflection over the sea), a plate lifting away to leave one ink (read as a 're-ink'), and the registration kick.
notes.9: Jitter, moiré, gradients and pure black/white match the original's concerns. The 'three halftones = mud' rule is missing.
notes.10: Shapes are built as multiply layers rather than plates with their own offsets, so only text misregisters. No kicks/drift and no per-plate gate.
notes.11: Inks are fixed by §3 and subjects confined to bands and discs, while the original's first free choice is the inks and what each plate means. Plate-based structures (subtraction, one ink left) are missing.
